## Species, phases and the two state vectors (`species`) {#sec-ch03-species-state}

### Summary

Every thermodynamic routine of kintera works on a list of species that is split into two groups: the gases first,
then the condensates. The list is read once from the `species` block of the YAML card, every reaction of the card
sorts its participants into one of the two groups, and from then on the position of a species in the list is its
index everywhere: in the mole-fraction vector of `ThermoX`, in the mass-fraction vector of `ThermoY`, in the
stoichiometric matrix and in the outputs of the saturation solvers of @sec-ch04. This section fixes that ordering,
the two state vectors and the conversions between them, because every later formula in this chapter and in
@sec-ch04 is written in those indices.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Define the species order (gases, then condensates), the mole-fraction state $x_i$ of `ThermoX` and the
mass-fraction state $y_i$ of `ThermoY`, and the conversions between them; the defining relation is
@eq-ch03-species-state-x-from-y.

**Data.** `species` entries of the card with `name`, `composition`, optional `phase`, `cv_R`, `u0_R`, `s0_R`; in
memory `vapor_ids`, `cloud_ids`, `mu` [$\mathrm{kg\,mol^{-1}}$]; $x_i$ on the last tensor axis, $y_i$ on the first.

**Placement.** At construction of `ThermoOptions` (card reading) and of `ThermoX` or `ThermoY` (`reset`); the
conversions run whenever a host code calls `compute` with one of the keys of @tbl-ch03-species-state-code.

**Activation.** Always; `phase: gas|liquid|solid` is optional and only the explicit way to put an inert gas or a gaseous
reaction product into the gas group.

**Guarantee / limits.** The conversions are exact algebra, closed to round-off; a card whose phases contradict its
reactions is refused at load.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `test_thermo` round trips on CPU and CUDA, float and double.
:::

Local symbols of this section, used throughout the chapter: $N$ species of which $N_{\mathrm g}$ are gases and
$N_{\mathrm c} = N - N_{\mathrm g}$ condensates, indexed by $i = 0, \dots, N-1$ in the order above (species $0$ is the
first gas, the reference species of the mass basis); $x_i$ the mole fraction of species $i$ among all species, gas and
condensed [-]; $y_i$ its mass fraction [-]; $c_i$ its molar concentration [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; $\rho_i$ its
partial density [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$] and $\rho = \sum_i \rho_i$ the total density; $M_i$ its molar mass
[$\mathrm{kg\,mol^{-1}}$]; $x_{\mathrm g} = \sum_{i < N_{\mathrm g}} x_i$ the gas share of the moles and
$c_{\mathrm g} = \sum_{i < N_{\mathrm g}} c_i$ the gas concentration. None of these is in the shared notation table
yet; they are proposed to the editor. The internal name of the mole basis is `ThermoX` and of the
mass basis `ThermoY`; the code calls the gas group `vapor` and the condensate group `cloud`.

### Derivation

The card lists species by name and elemental composition. The molar mass $M_i$ is the composition-weighted sum of the
element masses, and the optional caloric entries `cv_R`, `u0_R` and `s0_R` are stored as they are read (their meaning
is the subject of @sec-ch03-caloric and @sec-ch03-reference-state). A species that is named nowhere else is a gas
only if the card says `phase: gas`; otherwise the groups are inferred from the reactions: every nucleation reactant is
a gas, every nucleation product without `phase: gas` is a condensate, and the first species of the card is a gas (the
reference species). Within each group the species keep the card order. The result is the species vector of the whole
chapter,
$$
(\underbrace{x_0, x_1, \dots, x_{N_{\mathrm g}-1}}_{\text{gases}},\;
 \underbrace{x_{N_{\mathrm g}}, \dots, x_{N-1}}_{\text{condensates}}),
$$
and no routine infers an index from the text of a reaction.

`ThermoX` keeps mole fractions of *all* species, so that $\sum_{i=0}^{N-1} x_i = 1$ and the condensates are counted
in the moles; `ThermoY` keeps the mass fractions $y_1, \dots, y_{N-1}$ of every species except the reference species,
whose mass fraction is $y_0 = 1 - \sum_{i \ge 1} y_i$. The two are related through the molar masses. With
$y_i = x_i M_i / \sum_k x_k M_k$, dividing numerator and denominator by $M_0$ and eliminating $x_0 = 1 - \sum_{k\ge1}
x_k$ gives, for $i \ge 1$,
$$
x_i = \frac{y_i\,M_0/M_i}{1 + \sum_{k \ge 1} y_k\,(M_0/M_k - 1)}, \qquad x_0 = 1 - \sum_{i \ge 1} x_i,
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-state-x-from-y}
which is the form the code evaluates: @eq-ch03-species-state-x-from-y
is computed in `ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_xfrac` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_xfrac >}}),
with `inv_mu` holding $1/M_i$ and `mud` the reference mass $M_0$. The inverse map is the definition itself,
$$
y_i = \frac{x_i M_i}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1} x_k M_k}, \qquad i = 1, \dots, N-1,
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-state-y-from-x}
and @eq-ch03-species-state-y-from-x is computed in `ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_yfrac`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_yfrac >}}). That the two are inverses is checked
symbolically and numerically (check lines `[C1]` and `[C2]` of `species_state_check.py`).

The mass basis also needs the partial densities. Given the total density $\rho$ and the mass fractions,
$$
\rho_0 = \rho\,\Bigl(1 - \sum_{i \ge 1} y_i\Bigr), \qquad \rho_i = \rho\,y_i \quad (i \ge 1),
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-state-ivol}
and @eq-ch03-species-state-ivol is computed in `ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_ivol`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_yfrac_to_ivol >}}); the code calls the vector of partial densities
`ivol`. Its inverse $y_i = \rho_i / \sum_k \rho_k$ is `ThermoYImpl::_ivol_to_yfrac`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_ivol_to_yfrac >}}), and the molar concentrations follow as
$c_i = \rho_i / M_i$ wherever a caloric function needs them (`[C3]`).

The mole basis needs concentrations from $(T, p, x)$. For an ideal gas the gas-only mole fractions
$x_i / x_{\mathrm g}$ are the partial-pressure fractions, so
$$
c_i = \frac{x_i}{x_{\mathrm g}}\,\frac{p}{\mathcal R\,T} \quad (i < N_{\mathrm g}), \qquad
c_i = c_0\,\frac{x_i}{x_0} \quad (i \ge N_{\mathrm g}),
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-state-conc}
where the condensates are scaled from the reference gas so that the mole ratios of the input are kept.
@eq-ch03-species-state-conc is computed in `ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_conc`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_xfrac_to_conc >}}), whose Newton loop on the compressibility factor
is the subject of @sec-ch03-eos; with the ideal-gas factor it is the closed form above (`[C4]`). The reverse step, the
total density from concentrations, is $\rho = \sum_i c_i M_i$ in `ThermoXImpl::_conc_to_dens`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_conc_to_dens >}}).

Everything in this section is exact algebra; the only approximation is the ideal-gas relation in
@eq-ch03-species-state-conc, whose generalisation is @sec-ch03-eos. The check `species_state_check.py` verifies the
closed forms symbolically and the round trips to round-off.

### Numerical method

There is no iteration here. The two state vectors differ in layout as well as in basis, and the layout is what a host
code has to get right: `ThermoX` stores $x_i$ on the *last* tensor axis, shape $(\dots, 1 + n_y)$ with
$n_y = N - 1$, while `ThermoY` stores $y_i$ on the *first* axis, shape $(n_y, \dots)$, so that a hydrodynamic code
can hand over its tracer array without a copy. @fig-ch03-species-state-layout shows both for the species of
`tests/jupiter.yaml` (four gases, three condensates). Every conversion permutes the species axis to the front,
operates, and permutes back; the permutation is a view, not a copy.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-species-state-layout
#| fig-cap: "The two state vectors for the species of the Jupiter test card: mole fractions of all seven species on the last axis of `ThermoX` (top row) and mass fractions of the six non-reference species on the first axis of `ThermoY` (bottom row), where the reference species is implied by the remainder (hatched). Filled boxes are gases, white boxes condensates; the green arrows are the two conversion keys."
#| fig-alt: "Two rows of boxes: the upper row has seven boxes labelled dry, H2O, NH3, H2S, H2O(l), NH3(s), NH4SH(s) with indices 0 to 6; the lower row has a hatched box for the implied reference species followed by six boxes for the other species; arrows labelled Y->X and X->Y connect the rows."
#| echo: false
from kintera_report.ch03.figures.fig_species_state_layout import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The species groups are decided once, at option construction, by `ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_options.cpp ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}): it starts the gas set with the
first species of the card, adds the reactants and products of every nucleation, coagulation and evaporation reaction
through `add_to_vapor_cloud` ({{< code src/thermo/nucleation.cpp add_to_vapor_cloud >}}), then adds every species
with an explicit `phase`, refuses a species that would end up in both groups, sorts each group by card index and
copies the caloric data in that order. A `ThermoX` or `ThermoY` built from the options then calls
`check_dimensions` ({{< code src/species.cpp check_dimensions >}}) in its `reset` to make sure every per-species array
has exactly $N$ entries; the arrays an object built without a card may lack are filled with no-op defaults by
`populate_thermo` ({{< code src/species.cpp populate_thermo >}}).

: Code map of the species order and the state conversions. {#tbl-ch03-species-state-code}

Walk-through, in the order a host code meets it:

1. Load the card. `init_species_from_yaml` ({{< code src/species.cpp init_species_from_yaml overload=2 >}}) fills
   the process-global registry: names, phases, molar masses, `cv_R` (default $5/2$), `u0_R` (default 0), `s0_R`
   (default 0) and the NASA-9 record if the name is in the bundled database. A `phase` other than `gas`, `liquid` or
   `solid` is refused. The registry is global, which is why the kintera tests that load several cards run each in its
   own interpreter.
2. Build the options. `ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml` returns a null pointer when the card has no `reference-state`
   block; otherwise it reads the block (@sec-ch03-reference-state), the `dynamics/equation-of-state`
   block of @sec-ch03-eos and the reactions, and forms the two groups as described above. Three errors a user can
   hit here:
   `Gas species classified as cloud`, `Condensed species classified as gas` and
   `Conflicting gas/cloud classification`, each naming the species.
3. Build the module. `ThermoY` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}) registers the buffers
   `inv_mu` ($1/M_i$), `cv0`, `u0` and `stoich`; `ThermoX` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::reset >}})
   registers `mu` and `stoich`. Both refuse a nucleation reaction with a condensed reactant or without a condensed
   product.
4. Convert. `ThermoYImpl::compute` and `ThermoXImpl::compute` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::compute >}})
   dispatch on the key string; an unknown key throws `Unknown abbreviation`, and `Y->X`, `X->Y`, `V->Y`, `DY->V` check
   that the species axis has length $N$ or $N - 1$ (`mass fraction size mismatch`).

A minimal card and the conversions it enables, in the public Python API (@sec-ch11):

```python
import torch
from kintera import ThermoOptions, ThermoX, ThermoY
# species: dry, H2O, NH3, H2S | H2O(l), NH3(s), NH4SH(s)
op = ThermoOptions.from_yaml("tests/jupiter.yaml")
tx, ty = ThermoX(op), ThermoY(op)
yfrac = torch.full((6, 2, 3), 0.01, dtype=torch.float64)  # (n_y, ...)
xfrac = ty.compute("Y->X", [yfrac])                     # (..., 1 + n_y)
yback = tx.compute("X->Y", [xfrac])                     # round trip
```

these round trips is far looser than the algebra requires (the check reaches $10^{-16}$ in double), so it is a
smoke test of layout and device handling, not a precision claim. `test_declared_inert_gas_and_phase_reset` passed in
the recorded CPU run of the Python selection.[^ch03-species-state-pyrun]

### Limits

- The species registry is process-global: loading a second card with a different `species` list replaces it, and an
  options object built before the reload keeps its own copy of names and masses but not of the registry. Two cards in
  one process with different species are not a tested configuration (the kintera tests isolate them in subprocesses).
- The implicit classification (first species and nucleation reactants are gases) is the legacy path; a card with a
  gaseous reaction product (@sec-ch04) or an inert gas that appears in no reaction must say `phase: gas`,
  or that species is left out of the gas group silently (an inert gas) or refused (a product).
- `ThermoX` counts condensates in the mole fractions, so $x_i$ is not a gas-only mixing ratio and the `x_` columns of
  the examples must be read that way; `ThermoY` carries no explicit entry for the reference species, so a negative
  remainder $1 - \sum_{i\ge1} y_i$ is not detected here (it surfaces as a negative gas concentration in
  @sec-ch04).
- Not measured: the cost of the axis permutations on CUDA for large tracer arrays.
